# ReceivedBody in trillium_http - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/trillium-http/1.4.0/trillium_http/struct.ReceivedBody.html

`pub struct ReceivedBody<'conn, Transport> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A received http body

This type represents a body that will be read from the underlying transport, which it may either
borrow from a [ Conn](https://docs.rs/struct.Conn.html) or own.

```
let app = HttpTest::new(|mut conn| async move {
    let body = conn.request_body();
    let body_string = body.read_string().await.unwrap();
    conn.with_response_body(format!("received: {body_string}"))
});
app.get("/").block().assert_body("received: ");
app.post("/")
    .with_body("hello")
    .block()
    .assert_body("received: hello");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#bounds-checking)Bounds checking

Every `ReceivedBody` has a maximum length beyond which it will return an error, expressed as a
u64. To override this on the specific `ReceivedBody`, use [ ReceivedBody::with_max_len](https://docs.rs/struct.ReceivedBody.html#method.with_max_len) or

`ReceivedBody::set_max_len`The default maximum length is 10mb; see [ HttpConfig::received_body_max_len](https://docs.rs/struct.HttpConfig.html#method.received_body_max_len) to configure
this server-wide.

[§](https://docs.rs#large-chunks-small-read-buffers)Large chunks, small read buffers

Attempting to read a chunked body with a buffer that is shorter than the chunk size in hex will result in an error.

[Source](https://docs.rs/swansong/0.3.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/swansong/lib.rs.html#259)#### pub fn [guard_count](https://docs.rs#method.guard_count)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/swansong/0.3.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/swansong/lib.rs.html#259)

#### pub fn [guard_count](https://docs.rs#method.guard_count)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

The total number of outstanding `Guard`s in this Swansong’s subtree.

For a root or leaf Swansong with no children, this is just the Guards created
via this Swansong (and its clones). For a Swansong with children, it is the
sum of Guards held in this node plus all Guards in all descendant subtrees.
Child Swansong handles themselves are not counted as Guards; only real
`Guard` instances are.

This performs an `O(subtree)` walk; prefer not to call it in a hot path.

Create a child [ Swansong](https://docs.rs/struct.Swansong.html) linked to this parent.

The child can be independently shut down without affecting the parent. However, when
the parent is shut down, the child will also be shut down. The parent’s shutdown will
not be considered complete until the child [ Swansong](https://docs.rs/struct.Swansong.html) and any associated

[s are dropped.](https://docs.rs/swansong/0.3.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/swansong/implementation/shutdown_completion/struct.ShutdownCompletion.html)

`ShutdownCompletion`This supports multi-level hierarchies: a child can itself have children, forming a tree. Shutdown propagates downward through the entire tree.

[§](https://docs.rs#performance)Performance

Creating a child has O(n) cost where n is the number of live children, due to cleanup of stale internal references. This is suitable for most use cases but may not be ideal for very high-frequency child creation with many concurrent children.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-http3-server)Example: HTTP/3 server

```
let server = Swansong::new();
// Each connection gets its own child swansong
let connection = server.child();
// Connection can be shut down independently (e.g., on GOAWAY)
connection.shut_down();
// Or the entire server can shut down, which also stops all connections
// server.shut_down().await;
```
Attach a guard to the provided type, delaying shutdown until it drops.

This function returns a [ Guarded](https://docs.rs/swansong/0.3.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/swansong/implementation/guarded/struct.Guarded.html) wrapper type provides transparent implementations of
various traits like

[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/future/future/trait.Future.html)

`Future`[, as well as](https://docs.rs/futures-core/0.3.32/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/futures_core/stream/trait.Stream.html)

`Stream`[ing to the wrapped type. This is identical to moving a](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/deref/trait.Deref.html)

`Deref`[into the wrapped type, but sometimes it’s easier to compose the guard around a named future than to move the guard into the future. See](https://docs.rs/swansong/0.3.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/swansong/implementation/guard/struct.Guard.html)

`Guard`[for more information about trait implementations on](https://docs.rs/swansong/0.3.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/swansong/implementation/guarded/struct.Guarded.html)

`Guarded`

`Guarded`## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/swansong/0.3.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/swansong/lib.rs.html#320)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Drop-for-Swansong)If we are dropping the last `Swansong` handle to a **root** node, stop the
associated futures. Dropping the last handle to a **child** (non-root) node
does not signal shutdown: the parent remains the governing authority, and
the child stays in its current state until the parent propagates stop or
until all Guards in the child’s subset naturally drain.

# TypeSet in trillium_http - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/trillium-http/1.4.0/trillium_http/struct.TypeSet.html

`pub struct TypeSet(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

A collection for heterogenous types

Note that there is currently no way to iterate over the collection, as there may be types stored that cannot be named by the calling code

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/type-set/0.3.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/type_set/lib.rs.html#174)#### pub fn [with_capacity](https://docs.rs#method.with_capacity)(capacity: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [TypeSet](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeSet.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/type-set/0.3.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/type_set/lib.rs.html#174)

#### pub fn [with_capacity](https://docs.rs#method.with_capacity)(capacity: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [TypeSet](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeSet.html)

Create an empty `TypeSet` with space for at least `capacity` distinct types.

Preallocating avoids the incremental reallocations that occur as types are inserted, which is
worthwhile when the number of types is known ahead of time or when reusing a `TypeSet` across
many fill/[ clear](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeSet.html#method.clear) cycles.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
let mut set = type_set::TypeSet::with_capacity(2);
set.insert("hello");
set.insert(1usize);
assert_eq!(set.get::<&'static str>(), Some(&"hello"));
```
Remove all types from this `TypeSet`, retaining the allocated capacity for reuse.

This is the cheap way to reuse a `TypeSet` allocation: clearing and refilling avoids
reallocating the backing storage that constructing a fresh `TypeSet` would require.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
let mut set = type_set::TypeSet::new().with("hello").with(1usize);
set.clear();
assert!(set.is_empty());
assert_eq!(set.get::<&'static str>(), None);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/type-set/0.3.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/type_set/lib.rs.html#221)#### pub fn [shrink_to_fit](https://docs.rs#method.shrink_to_fit)(&mut self)

[Source](https://docs.rs/type-set/0.3.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/type_set/lib.rs.html#221)

#### pub fn [shrink_to_fit](https://docs.rs#method.shrink_to_fit)(&mut self)

Shrink the capacity of this `TypeSet` as much as possible.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example

set.shrink_to_fit();

#### pub fn [get_or_insert_with](https://docs.rs#method.get_or_insert_with)<T>(&mut self, default: impl [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)() -> T) -> [&mut T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

Get a value from this `TypeSet` or populate it with the provided default function.

Identical to `Entry::or_insert_with`

Prefer this to [ TypeSet::get_or_insert](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeSet.html#method.get_or_insert) when building type T is expensive, since it will only be
executed when T is absent.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-10)Example

```
let mut set = type_set::TypeSet::new();
assert_eq!(set.get_or_insert_with(|| String::from("hello")), "hello");
assert_eq!(set.get_or_insert_with::<String>(|| panic!("this is never called")), "hello");
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/type-set/0.3.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/type_set/lib.rs.html#383)#### pub fn [get_or_insert_default](https://docs.rs#method.get_or_insert_default)<T>(&mut self) -> [&mut T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/type-set/0.3.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/type_set/lib.rs.html#383)

#### pub fn [get_or_insert_default](https://docs.rs#method.get_or_insert_default)<T>(&mut self) -> [&mut T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

Ensure a value is present by filling with `Default::default`

Identical to [ Entry::or_default](https://docs.rs/type-set/0.3.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/type_set/entry/enum.Entry.html#method.or_default).

[§](https://docs.rs#example-11)Example

```
let mut set = type_set::TypeSet::new().with(10usize);
let ten: usize = *set.get_or_insert_default();
assert_eq!(ten, 10);
```
Merge another `TypeSet` into this one, replacing any collisions

[§](https://docs.rs#example-12)Example

```
let mut set_a = type_set::TypeSet::new().with(8u8).with("hello");
let set_b = type_set::TypeSet::new().with(32u32).with("world");
set_a.merge(set_b);
assert_eq!(set_a.get::<u8>(), Some(&8));
assert_eq!(set_a.get::<u32>(), Some(&32));
assert_eq!(set_a.get::<&'static str>(), Some(&"world"));
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/trillium_http/upgrade.rs.html#447-508)#### pub async fn [send_trailers](https://docs.rs#method.send_trailers)(self, trailers: [Headers](https://docs.rs/headers/struct.Headers.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/io/error/type.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/trillium_http/upgrade.rs.html#447-508)

#### pub async fn [send_trailers](https://docs.rs#method.send_trailers)(self, trailers: [Headers](https://docs.rs/headers/struct.Headers.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/io/error/type.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html)>

Emit trailing headers and finish the outbound stream. Consumes `self`; further
writes are statically prevented.

Per-protocol behavior:

- HTTP/1.1 with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`: writes the last-chunk marker (`0\r\n`), the trailer section, and a final CRLF, then closes the transport.
- HTTP/2: enqueues a trailing `HEADERS`frame with`END_STREAM`via the connection driver and returns. The driver finishes the stream after draining any pending DATA frames.
- HTTP/3: encodes a trailing `HEADERS`frame via QPACK, writes it to the stream, then closes the stream (QUIC`FIN`).
- HTTP/1.1 without chunked encoding (raw upgrade, CONNECT tunnel, websocket-over-h1):
trailers can’t be expressed on the wire; dropped with a `log::warn!`and`Ok(())`returned.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns the underlying [ io::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/io/error/struct.Error.html) when the wire write fails,

`BrokenPipe` if
the stream has already been closed, and `NotConnected` if the carried
`ProtocolSession` is missing the expected driver for h2/h3.## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)
